# Bluetooth Connectivity Guide for Android and iOS Devices

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67080905769fb0fc5f37e534/68811aa38be51ef8e31c5933_66bd147b8c0814014114f532_Arrow%202%20(3)%201.svg)\\

Below are some simple troubleshooting steps to help you resolve common Bluetooth connectivity issues and ensure your device works seamlessly.

In This Article

### **Table of Contents**

- Enabling Bluetooth on Android
- Enabling Bluetooth on iOS
- Enabling Bluetooth within an App on Android
- Enabling Bluetooth within an App on iOS

### **Enabling Bluetooth on Android:**

1. Unlock your Android device and locate the Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap on "Connections" or "Connections & Network."
3. Look for and tap on "Bluetooth."
4. Toggle the switch next to "Bluetooth" to the right. When it turns blue, Bluetooth is now enabled.

To the top

### **Enabling Bluetooth on iOS:**

1. Unlock your iOS device and find the Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap on "Bluetooth." It's usually near the top of the menu.
3. Toggle the switch next to "Bluetooth" to the right. When it turns green, Bluetooth is now enabled.

To the top

### **Enabling Bluetooth within an App on Android:**

1. Unlock your Android device and open the "Settings" app.
2. Scroll down and select "Apps" or "Application Manager."
3. Find and tap on the specific app for which you want to enable Bluetooth.
4. Inside the app settings, look for "Permissions" or "App Permissions."
5. Toggle the switch next to "Bluetooth" to the right to enable Bluetooth for the chosen app.

To the top

### **Enabling Bluetooth within an App on iOS:**

1. Unlock your iOS device and locate the "Settings" app.
2. Scroll down and tap on "Privacy," then select "Bluetooth."
3. Find and tap on the specific app for which you want to enable Bluetooth.
4. Toggle the switch next to Bluetooth to the right, ensuring it turns green to enable Bluetooth for the chosen app.

To the top

### **Disabling Bluetooth on Android:**

1. Open the Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap on "Connections" or "Connections & Network."
3. Look for and tap on "Bluetooth."
4. Toggle the switch next to "Bluetooth" to the left. When it turns gray, Bluetooth is now disabled.

To the top

### **Disabling Bluetooth on iOS:**

1. Open the Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap on "Bluetooth."
3. Toggle the switch next to "Bluetooth" to the left. When it turns white, Bluetooth is now disabled.

To the top

We hope these steps help resolve any Bluetooth connectivity issues you may encounter. If you have any further questions or need assistance, please don't hesitate to contact the **Wellinks Help Line at 1-877-220-8935.**
